chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from his brother Ja'far ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a woman, so he associated in the bequest a child along with her. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is allowed, and the woman enforces the bequest and does not wait for the adulthood of the child. So when the child reaches adulthood, it is not for him to reject it, except for what was from alteration or change. Indeed, he has the right to return it to what the deceased had bequeathed to him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a minor child in a joint bequest with an adult woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of immediate executability of a bequest when a minor is included, allowing the adult beneficiary (here, the woman) to act without delay for the minor's benefit. It clarifies that the minor retains the right of 'option' (ikhtiyar) upon reaching maturity to ratify the adult's management or reject unauthorized alterations, ensuring the deceased's final wishes are preserved. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the minor's financial interests while facilitating efficient estate administration.
